Definition: from G2309 and G2356; voluntary (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety, i.e. sanctimony:--will worship.
BiblicalUsage: Ethelothrēskeía means will-worship — a religion of one's own making, a piety God never asked for. It occurs just once, where Paul warns that self-made religion has a show of wisdom but no honour against the satisfying of the flesh. The word names worship invented by the worshipper.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ethelothrēskeía is a warning I need: worship I invent for myself may look wise, but it holds nothing back in me.
